comparator.name: History
comparator.sourceNotes: The official course table and the 2026–2027 degree guide identify the 180 EC full-time degree. The public course table supplies the full three-year sequence, including 12 EC of second-year and 30 EC of third-year free choice. The 12 EC thesis is separate from introductory and advanced history research and the final reading assessment. No formal track is selected.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad historical option and the heritage and public-memory option are coherent and differ by at least 30 EC. The period-specialist direction has too little sustained ancient and medieval historical progression in available course content to form a coherent third option.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both survey modern historical change. UCR examines political, social and cultural developments from 1815.
Both examine historical change across regions. UCR focuses on empires and how historians explain their power and institutions.
Both examine early modern cross-cultural change. UCR focuses on Renaissance art and exchange around the Mediterranean.
Both examine classical Greek society. UCR focuses on the material evidence of early democracy, while UvA covers Greek and Roman antiquity more broadly.

notes.text: UvA combines broad historical study with dedicated work in digital sources, historical theory, primary-source research and a required thesis. UCR combines history with archaeology, art history and media. The options give different ways to study the past and how it is presented.

audience.programmeDescription: History at the University of Amsterdam covers historical periods, historiography and the study of primary sources. Students develop independent research through seminars and a thesis, with room for electives.
audience.comparisonExplanation: The closest UCR option combines history with art, archaeology, literature and politics. The second focuses on how museums, media and communities interpret the past.
